dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes by a factor of three between sectors and from one transit to the next, including a negative depth, which a planet cannot do. Its duration is too long for a central transit on this small M dwarf and the star spins with the same period but with a few-thousand ppm of spot signal. Together this matches stellar variability, not a stable 1.43 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent (one at -135 ppm, one at 3230 ppm vs mean 1305 ppm), with share_of_top_3 0.717 and only 7 transits, inconsistent with a stable planet transit.

Depth really changes between sectors (p_constant 9.012272437397045e-06, p_constant 0.000009134) with depths 1446, 1416, 742, 984, 2342 ppm - a factor ~3 change within same SPOC 2-min product, not a calibration offset.
Duration 3.499 h is longer than central 2.237 h and fit implies high impact parameter and stellar-density mismatch expected for an eclipse, not a planet transit on a 0.365 Rsun M dwarf.

Rotation detected at 13.303 d (amplitude 2725 ppm in sector 68) essentially identical to signal period 13.5 d with large spotted variability amplitude, phase_curve amplitude 67.66 ppm small but variability present, favouring spot-induced variability / alias over planet.
